review_text: This is the Dunkin’ Donuts San Pedro branch—definitely one of the busiest, especially during the holidays. Despite the crowd, the service remains fast and organized. Their donuts and drinks are not expensive, making it an easy choice when you want something quick and satisfying. The treats are always fresh, consistent, and comforting. What I really appreciate is the staff—they’re friendly, accommodating, and still manage to smile even when the line gets long. A reliable spot for a sweet break in the middle of the city.

Dunkin’ is one of my go-to places when I want something quick, delicious, and budget friendly, especially their donuts. This branch has always been consistent when it comes to food quality, service, and even the overall atmosphere of the place. Everything feels smooth and reliable every visit. Overall, I had a great time here.

Stopped here at Dunkin’ on my way home from the gym for a cold drink and ordered an iced Spanish Latte. Staff was friendly and helpful but were wearing masks which made it difficult to hear, but not a major issue. There were 5 or 6 people inside enjoying their drinks and the place was clean and inviting. Really enjoyed my iced latte when I got home and it is priced fairly. Close and convenient for me.

This is always a great place to drink your morning brew. They just opened this Dinkins, the coffee is the same all over the world, however I think the water here makes a big difference as the quality of the water is also excellent here in Davao city. I have only one concern here. It appears they installed a handicap ramp, howere there is a step into the store. Maybe this was a mistake in the planning, but maybe a problem with handicapped people. The coffee is still under a buck, even with the increased price.

Dunkin’ is always my favorite for munchkins and donuts. Whenever I visit new places, like here in Davao City, I make sure to stop by a Dunkin’ store to grab some coffee and donuts. I never forget to buy munchkins for my kids too. I always love it!

Foreigner here, food was decent but I felt uncomfortable and disrespected by security and staff because the looks I received and they would rudely laugh while staring at me… I’ve lived in Philippines 4 months already and I know the difference if it’s a friendly laugh/look or “I’m judging you” laugh/look. They need to be careful of their words because they expect that I don’t speak visaya, but maybe I do speak… they should have more respect for a foreigner.

This place helped me when my wife was pregnant with our first child. Like, where can you buy Bunwich in the middle of the night? It also has access to Mercury Drug right infront, so I can park at Dunkin' buy NANHW for the baby accross the street and bring home a box of donuts for the us. Now, everyone wants donuts, I have to get 3 Boston Kremes because the kids want what I want.

Rude service from two of the people at the counter. They were dismissive, were making faces, had terrible body language, and walked away while I was talking. I love Dunkin but will never go to this one again. I’m surprised management allows such behavior and does not screen the workers to avoid these type of people.
